takeaways.label: Integrated model gains traction
takeaways.text: Sai converted a second large pharma relationship into a strategic, end-to-end engagement and started integrated discovery programs with two large pharma customers, validating the full-service CRO-CDMO thesis.

takeaways.label: Capacity build-out stays on track
takeaways.text: Bidar's 220 KL expansion is ready for commercial batches, while the second 225 KL block slipped to Q3 FY28 as the company prioritized other customer capability builds.

takeaways.label: Biotech green shoots appear
takeaways.text: Enquiry uptick from biotech customers, particularly for integrated engagements in new modalities like peptides, signals a potential funding-cycle revival.

takeaways.label: Second-half skew reaffirmed
takeaways.text: Management expects a stronger H2, but declined to quantify the ramp.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the two new integrated discovery programs convert to material revenue, the pace of commercial batch commencement at Bidar, and any further biotech enquiry conversion.

points.label: Model validation
points.text: The first end-to-end integrated collaboration with a top-tier market-cap pharma company commenced operations, and a second large pharma relationship was converted into a similar strategic engagement this quarter.

points.label: Discovery integration
points.text: Integrated discovery programs were started with two large pharma customers; these programs are currently small but demonstrate the model's appeal.

points.label: Pipeline ambition
points.text: Management is in discussions with a few more large pharma customers to extend the integrated strategic engagement model, aiming to build a robust, consistent, and predictable long-term pipeline.

points.label: No revenue visibility offered
points.text: Management explicitly declined to provide revenue potential or wallet share for these collaborations, stating "We don't give any guidance in that count. We've never done and never will."

points.label: Pace caveat
points.text: Contract negotiations move slowly and may not mature; management noted "it may or may not mature as well. There is a conversation. They might not mature."

quotes.text: Krishna Kanumuri: "I think the important thing here... to look at is the fact that we are the only company which has significant scale in all three dimensions, so discovery, development, and commercial."

points.label: Bidar ready
points.text: The expanded small molecule manufacturing capacity of around 220 KL at Bidar is now ready, with final quality trials underway ahead of commencing commercial batches; this capacity is expected to be revenue-accretive in the current year.

points.label: Second block recalibrated
points.text: Commissioning of the additional 225 KL capacity is now expected by Q3 FY28, a delay from the earlier timeline, because other capability needed by a couple of large pharma customers was prioritized. Management does not expect this to affect FY28 revenue commitments.

points.label: H1 capex incurred
points.text: ₹621 crores spent in H1 FY27 (₹358 crores in Q2); the company remains on track with the overall FY27 capex plan of ₹1,100–₹1,300 crores.

points.label: Next greenfield
points.text: Design work on a new manufacturing site in Telangana has commenced; ground-breaking is expected in Q4 FY27 (January/February). The land parcel is larger than the current site in Bidar and can support capacity higher than what we have here, with multimodalities.

points.label: Funding stance
points.text: Management is comfortable with current leverage and committed to not starving the business of capex; if needed, it will return to the market or take on debt. A three-to-four-year capex guidance was declined.

quotes.text: Siva Chittor: "This business is a service business unless you put up capacity and unless you're available and be ready, customers will move up their products from a clinical phase to some other supplier in commercial. What you will get to hear is potentials and possibilities."

points.label: Late-phase pipeline
points.text: Phase III and pre-registration programs stood at 14 as of June; one molecule moved out and one came in, leaving the count flat. The 11 figure in the Q1 presentation was as of March 31, 2026; three molecules were added subsequently.

points.label: Commercial molecules
points.text: One molecule moved from late-phase to commercial during the quarter, and one lateral entry was added, bringing total commercial molecules to 34. The discovery-to-market count remains at 5.

points.label: CRO utilization
points.text: The new CRO block was at 85–90% utilization as mentioned in the previous quarter; the company is already adding more CRO capacity.

points.label: Headcount growth
points.text: Headcount increased to around 4,400 at the end of September, reflecting people-related growth to support the business.

points.label: Peptide progress
points.text: The first peptide development lab was commissioned during the quarter; additional peptide development labs are under construction and expected in the next few months.

points.label: Peptide plant timeline
points.text: Design work for the new peptide plant in Telangana is ongoing; ground-breaking is expected in Q4 (January/February) once the master plan is complete.

points.label: ADC and bioconjugation
points.text: Discovery sites are active; Class 6 containment labs for cross-development are coming online soon; CMC labs are almost online this year.

points.label: Gradual migration
points.text: Management expects a gradual shift to newer modalities over the next two to three years as customers get comfortable with delivery and relationships, not a sudden shift overnight. India will be a player in most modalities because of small-molecule backbones.

points.label: Technology evolution
points.text: Technology in peptides and oligonucleotides is changing dramatically; the company is focused on ensuring its technology is ready and evolving with the direction of the field.

points.label: Pharma-led growth
points.text: Over the last 10–15 months, growth in large pharma has been a big factor driving overall growth; the CRO pharma split reached 40% as of the end of 2026, up from minimal presence a few years ago.

points.label: Biotech revival signs
points.text: An uptick in enquiries from biotech customers was witnessed, with many enquiries for integrated engagements in new modalities, specifically peptides. Biotech funding is in a mid-phase cycle of selling late-stage assets; new company formation is expected to start once that cycle completes, with early green shoots from increased IPOs and acquisitions.

points.label: India's strategic shift
points.text: Management observed that large pharma companies are now thinking about how to become strategic with one or two companies in India, moving beyond India's historical role as a tactical supplier for specific projects.

points.label: Raw material pressure
points.text: A modest increase in raw material costs, particularly certain solvents and chemicals, arose from the ongoing Middle East situation; supply-chain teams ensured continuity, and the company is working with customers to recover incremental costs.

quotes.text: Krishna Kanumuri: "India was a more of a tactical supplier where they would come for some projects. But now almost every large pharma is thinking about how do you become strategic with a few, maybe one or two companies in India."

points.label: Net positive for India
points.text: Management sees AI as a net positive for India's CDMO industry; better-quality tools for process optimization and process development make the company more competitive.

points.label: No budget compression
points.text: Pharma counterparts have told management that AI's outcome will probably be more molecules rather than reducing budgets, depending on success. More molecules in the clinic help the development side.

points.label: Discovery services resilient
points.text: Management does not see a significant AI impact on discovery services because, regardless of design, molecules must still be made and tested.

quotes.text: Krishna Kanumuri: "I think AI impact on discovery services will not be significant, because end of the day, I think no matter what the design is, you have to continue to make the molecules and test the molecules."

items.title: Bidar capacity expansion
items.text: The first 225 KL block at Unit IV, Bidar (~220 KL expanded small-molecule capacity) is ready with final quality trials underway, expected to be revenue-accretive in FY27, taking the site from 700 KL toward 1,150 KL. With Q2 FY27 utilization at 67% and plants considered full at ~70-75%, the new blocks remove the main near-term capacity bottleneck on a ₹2,371 cr revenue base.

items.title: Integrated CRDMO partnerships
items.text: The first end-to-end integrated collaboration with a top-tier pharma company is fully functional from Q3 FY27, and a second large pharma relationship was converted to the same model in Q2 FY27, with more in discussion. Management expects the integrated portion of the CRO to drive growth over the next two years, mirroring the WuXi/Pharmaron strategic-relationship model.

items.title: CMC late-phase pipeline
items.text: The pipeline stands at 34 commercial and 14 late-phase molecules as of Q2 FY27, with the Phase III/pre-registration count up from ~6 a year earlier to 11, and four commercial contracts being added in FY27, three as commercial supplies. Late-phase molecules convert to multi-year commercial revenue as they win approvals - two more customers have regulatory milestones this financial year.

items.title: CRO large pharma expansion
items.text: CRO revenue grew 28% YoY in Q2 FY27 and the pharma mix reached 48% in FY26 from 38% in FY25, with new discovery capacity added in Q1 FY27 immediately sold out and already running at 85-90% utilization. Management is already adding more CRO capacity to serve the ~50/50 pharma/biotech target, with pharma driving growth for the next couple of years.

items.title: Choutuppal greenfield site
items.text: Design work has commenced on a ~40-acre Telangana campus designed for ~1,400 KL of reactor capacity - larger than Bidar - with groundbreaking expected in Q4 FY27 and dedicated early/mid-stage plus peptide capacity in the design. This is the main capacity lever for FY29-30, adding roughly a second Bidar-sized manufacturing base.

items.title: Peptides build-out
items.text: The first dedicated peptide development lab was commissioned as of Q2 FY27 with more labs under construction, and a peptide manufacturing plant at Choutuppal is targeted operational in 2028 on total spend under ₹300 cr. Commercial peptide capacity from 2028 lets Sai capture GLP-1-era demand where it currently has no manufacturing revenue.

items.title: Process R&D capacity doubling
items.text: The 100,000 sq ft Process R&D Block at Unit 2, Hyderabad - 140 fume hoods, kilo lab and formulation development - was scheduled for commissioning by September 2026, nearly doubling process R&D capacity. More development capacity feeds the funnel of molecules that later convert into commercial CDMO contracts.

items.title: ADC / bioconjugation capability
items.text: OEB 6 containment labs for ADC process development complete in October 2026, and an XDC Center of Excellence covering payloads, linkers and conjugation is close to opening. Several pharma customers already doing ADC discovery with Sai want to expand, underpinning future capacity filling.
